statements.text: a driver SHOULD use low beams WHEN the driver is less than 60 m behind another vehicle UNLESS the driver is passing it

sources.quote: Use your low beams when you are less than 60 metres behind another vehicle unless you are passing it.

statements.note: The force is advisory because the handbook uses the imperative 'Use' without legal markers like 'must' or 'illegal'. The condition 'unless you are passing it' is an exception in the same passage, so it is written as an UNLESS clause.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD keep to the right of the road or in the right-hand lane on multi-lane roads UNLESS the driver wants to turn left OR the driver wants to pass another vehicle

sources.quote: Keep to the right of the road or in the right-hand lane on multi-lane roads unless you want to turn left or pass another vehicle.

flags.note: The handbook uses the imperative 'Keep' without explicit legal wording (e.g., 'must' or 'illegal'), so the force is treated as advisory.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a vehicle WHEN the vehicle is stopped at a crosswalk BECAUSE a stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing

sources.quote: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. A stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing.

statements.text: a driver MUST maintain a minimum distance of 1 m between the vehicle and the cyclist WHEN passing a cyclist AND it is [?practical] IF VIOLATED a fine AND 2 demerit points

sources.quote: When passing a cyclist, drivers of motor vehicles must maintain a minimum distance of one metre, where practical between their vehicle and the cyclist.
Failure to do so may result in a fine and an additional two demerit points on the driver’s record.

flags.note: The handbook does not define what makes maintaining the distance impractical.

statements.note: The penalty in m57 refers to the duty in m56, so they are joined.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD change lanes to pass a cyclist WHEN passing a cyclist AND it is [?possible]

sources.quote: Whenever possible, you should change lanes to pass.

flags.note: The handbook does not define the conditions under which changing lanes is possible.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT sound the horn unnecessarily WHEN overtaking a cyclist BECAUSE it may frighten them and cause them to lose control

sources.quote: Do not sound your horn unnecessarily when you are overtaking a cyclist. It may frighten them and cause them to lose control.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD tap the horn quickly and lightly WHEN the driver feels that the driver must use the horn to overtake a cyclist AND the driver is still some distance away from the cyclist

sources.quote: If you feel that you must use your horn, tap it quickly and lightly while you are still some distance away from the cyclist.

flags.note: No specific distance is given for how far away the driver should be.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut in front closely WHEN passing a large vehicle BECAUSE it reduces the space cushion large vehicles require in order to stop safely

sources.quote: When passing a large vehicle, do not cut in front closely. Not only is this discourteous, it is dangerous; it reduces the space cushion large vehicles require in order to stop safely.

flags.note: No specific distance is given for what constitutes cutting in front closely.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD allow more room WHEN passing a large vehicle

sources.quote: Allow more room when passing a large vehicle.

flags.note: No specific amount of extra room is defined.

statements.text: FACT a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence THAT may affect a driver's ability to control the vehicle WHEN passing the large vehicle

sources.quote: Due to various factors such as air pressure and airflow, a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence. This may affect your ability to control your vehicle when passing a large one.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD stay well back AND SHOULD NOT pass a farm vehicle UNTIL it is [?safe] to do so

sources.quote: Stay well back and do not pass until it is safe to do so.

flags.note: No objective measure of safety is given.

statements.note: The context implies this applies to farm machinery, as per the heading.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD maintain a [?safe] following distance AND SHOULD NOT pass a horse-drawn vehicle UNTIL it is [?safe] to do so

sources.quote: Maintain a safe following distance and only pass when it is safe to do so.

flags.note: No objective measure of safety or distance is given.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD give as much distance between the vehicle and the horse-drawn vehicle as possible WHEN passing a horse-drawn vehicle BECAUSE passing too closely could scare or startle the horse, causing it to change direction suddenly on the roadway

sources.quote: When passing, give as much distance between you and them as possible. Passing too closely could scare or startle the horse, causing it to change direction suddenly on the roadway.

flags.note: No specific distance is defined.

statements.text: a driver MUST stop WHEN approaching a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing AND the driver is behind the bus OR approaching the bus from the front

sources.quote: You must stop whenever you approach a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front.

statements.force_from: context (penalty in c5: "can be fined heavily and get six demerit points")
statements.text: a driver MUST stop at least 20 m away WHEN the driver is coming from behind a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing

sources.quote: If you are coming from behind the bus, stop at least 20 metres away.
If you don't stop, you can be fined heavily and get six demerit points for a first offence.

statements.note: The force is legal because the penalty in c5 applies to failing to stop for a school bus.

statements.force_from: context (penalty in c5: "can be fined heavily and get six demerit points")
statements.text: a driver MUST NOT go WHEN the driver has stopped for a school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing UNTIL the bus moves OR the lights have stopped flashing

sources.quote: Do not go until the bus moves or the lights have stopped flashing.
If you don't stop, you can be fined heavily and get six demerit points for a first offence.

statements.note: The force is legal because the penalty in c5 applies to failing to stop for a school bus.

statements.text: EXCEPTION TO p04:s1 WHEN the road has a median strip AND the driver is approaching the bus from the front

sources.quote: If you are on a road with a median strip, only vehicles coming from behind the bus must stop.

statements.text: FACT school bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that have illegally passed a school bus

sources.quote: In Ontario, school bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that have illegally passed a school bus.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass any vehicle WHEN the vehicle is within 30 m of a pedestrian crossover

sources.quote: You must not pass any vehicle within 30 metres of a pedestrian crossover.

statements.text: DEFINE passing IS changing lanes TO move past a slower vehicle

sources.quote: Passing is changing lanes to move past a slower vehicle.

statements.text: FACT motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds often need to pull to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions or to be seen by other drivers

sources.quote: Motorcycles, bicycles, limited-speed motorcycles and mopeds often need to pull to the left or right side of their lane to avoid dangerous road conditions or to be seen by other drivers.

flags.note: Frequency is not specified.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a motorcycle, bicycle, limited-speed motorcycle or moped in the same lane WHEN the vehicle pulls to the left or right side of its lane

sources.quote: Do not take this as an invitation to pass in the same lane.

statements.note: The condition 'pulls to the side' is derived from the previous sentence in the same passage.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD pass a motorcycle, bicycle, limited-speed motorcycle or moped by changing lanes WHEN the driver wants to pass the vehicle

sources.quote: If you do want to pass these vehicles, do so by changing lanes.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD ensure there is enough space and time to complete the move safely BEFORE beginning to pass a vehicle

sources.quote: Before beginning, be sure you have enough space and time to complete the move safely.

flags.note: No specific measure for space or time is given.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT overtake and pass another vehicle UNLESS the driver is [?sure] the driver can do so without danger to the driver or others

sources.quote: Never overtake and pass another vehicle unless you are sure you can do so without danger to yourself or others.

flags.note: Subjective certainty; no observable test.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a moving snow plow

sources.quote: Don't pass moving snow plows under any conditions.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a vehicle WHEN the driver is in doubt about whether it is safe to pass

sources.quote: If in doubt, do not pass.

flags.note: Subjective state; no observable test.

statements.text: TO pass a vehicle

steps.text: use the left-turn signal to show that the driver wants to pass AND check that the way is clear ahead and behind BEFORE moving into the passing lane

watch for bicycles and small vehicles that may be hidden from view in front of the vehicle the driver is about to pass AND watch for vehicles that may be turning left in front of the driver AND watch for vehicles or pedestrians entering the road from another road or driveway

change lanes ONLY IF the driver has signalled AND after overtaking, signal that the driver wants to move back into the lane the driver started from AND when the driver can see the entire front of the vehicle the driver is passing in the inside mirror, make the lane change

sources.quote: Here are the steps for passing a vehicle:

statements.note: The procedure covers the main steps for passing. Specific warnings like 'do not cut off' are separate rules.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut off a vehicle by suddenly moving in front of it WHEN passing the vehicle

sources.quote: Be careful not to cut off a vehicle by suddenly moving in front of it.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT race the vehicle being passed AND SHOULD go back to the original lane WHEN the vehicle being passed speeds up

sources.quote: If the vehicle you are passing speeds up, do not race. Go back to your original lane.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT speed up WHEN another driver is trying to pass the driver BECAUSE it is dangerous

sources.quote: And do not speed up when another driver is trying to pass you. It is unlawful and dangerous.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass a vehicle WHEN the driver is within 30 m of a pedestrian crossover

sources.quote: Passing within 30 metres of a pedestrian crossover is not permitted.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass a vehicle to the left of the centreline WHEN the driver is within 30 m of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel

sources.quote: Passing left of a centreline is not permitted 30 metres from a bridge, viaduct or tunnel.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT attempt to pass a vehicle WHEN approaching the crest of a hill OR on a curve WHERE the driver's vision of oncoming traffic is obstructed AND there is not enough clear distance ahead to pass in safety

sources.quote: Don't attempt to pass when approaching the crest of a hill or on a curve where your vision of oncoming traffic is obstructed and there is not enough clear distance ahead to pass in safety.

flags.note: No specific measure for clear distance is given.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD WATCH FOR people suddenly opening doors OR doors opened to load and unload WHEN passing parked vehicles

sources.quote: When passing parked vehicles, watch carefully for people suddenly opening doors or for doors opened to load and unload.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD move to the right AND let faster traffic pass in safety WHEN faster traffic wants to pass the driver

sources.quote: When faster traffic wants to pass you, move to the right and let it pass in safety.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD pay attention to oncoming traffic AND move closer to the right side of the lane AND be prepared to slow down to let the passing driver get in front of the driver more quickly to prevent a collision WHEN being passed on an undivided road WHERE the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane

sources.quote: When being passed on an undivided road where the passing driver has pulled into the opposite lane, pay attention to oncoming traffic and move closer to the right side of the lane. Be prepared to slow down to let the passing driver get in front of you more quickly to prevent a collision.

statements.text: FACT on many high-speed roads with three or more lanes in each direction, trucks are not allowed to drive in the far left-hand lane, making the lane next to it the truck passing lane

sources.quote: On many high-speed roads with three or more lanes in each direction, trucks are not allowed to drive in the far left-hand lane. This means that the lane next to it is the truck passing lane.

flags.note: Scope is not specified.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD move into the right-hand lane as soon as the driver can WHEN the driver is in the truck passing lane AND a truck wants to pass the driver

sources.quote: If you are in this lane and a truck wants to pass, move into the right-hand lane as soon as you can.

flags.span: as soon as the driver can
flags.note: No specific time or condition for 'as soon as' is given.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD be very careful WHEN passing other vehicles at night

sources.quote: Be very careful when you pass other vehicles at night.

statements.text: TO pass a vehicle at night WHEN the way is clear

steps.text: switch the headlights to low beams AS the driver approaches a vehicle from behind
signal AND check the mirrors and blind spot AND pull out to pass AND switch on the high beams AS the driver moves alongside the vehicle being passed
pull back into the right lane WHEN the driver can see all of the front of the vehicle being passing in the rear view mirror AND signal

sources.quote: If you have to pass and the way is clear, follow these steps:

statements.text: FACT some roads have special passing or climbing lanes that let slower vehicles move into the right-hand lane so that faster ones can pass safely in the left lane

sources.quote: Some roads have special passing or climbing lanes. These lanes let slower vehicles move into the right-hand lane so that faster ones can pass safely in the left lane.

flags.note: Scope is not specified.

statements.text: FACT an advance sign tells drivers they will soon have a chance to pass AND another sign warns when the lane is ending so drivers in the right-hand lane can begin to merge safely with traffic in the left-hand lane

sources.quote: An advance sign tells drivers they will soon have a chance to pass. Another sign warns when the lane is ending so drivers in the right-hand lane can begin to merge safely with traffic in the left-hand lane.

statements.text: a driver MAY drive on the right shoulder ONLY IF the driver is passing a vehicle turning left AND the shoulder is paved

sources.quote: You may drive on the right shoulder only to pass a vehicle turning left and only if the shoulder is paved.

statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass a vehicle on the left shoulder

sources.quote: You may not pass on the left shoulder, paved or not.

statements.text: FACT most passing is done on the left

sources.quote: Most passing is done on the left.

flags.note: Proportion is not specified.

statements.text: a driver MAY pass a vehicle on the right WHEN the road is a multi-lane road OR the road is a one-way road OR the vehicle being passed is a streetcar OR the vehicle being passed is a left-turning vehicle

sources.quote: You may pass on the right on multi-lane or one-way roads and when overtaking a streetcar or a left-turning vehicle.

statements.text: FACT passing on the right can be more dangerous than passing on the left

sources.quote: Passing on the right can be more dangerous than passing on the left.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD wait for the vehicle to move to the right AND SHOULD NOT suddenly change lanes and pass on the right WHEN the driver is in the left most lane AND a slower vehicle is in front of the driver

sources.quote: If you are driving in the left most lane with a slower vehicle in front of you, wait for the vehicle to move to the right. Do not suddenly change lanes and pass on the right; the driver in front may realize you want to pass and move to the right at the same time you do.

statements.text: a driver MUST pass a streetcar on the right UNLESS the driver is driving on a one-way road

sources.quote: You must pass streetcars on the right unless you are driving on a one-way road.

statements.text: a driver MUST stay at least 2 m behind the rear doors of a stopped streetcar WHEN at a streetcar stop AND passengers are getting off or on UNLESS an area has been set aside for streetcar passengers at the stop

sources.quote: At streetcar stops, stay at least two metres behind the rear doors where passengers are getting off or on. This rule does not apply at stops where an area has been set aside for streetcar passengers.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD pass areas set aside for streetcar passengers at a [?reasonable] speed AND be prepared for pedestrians to make sudden or unexpected moves

sources.quote: Always pass these areas at a reasonable speed and be prepared for pedestrians to make sudden or unexpected moves.

flags.note: No specific speed limit is given.

statements.note: The phrase 'these areas' refers to the areas set aside for streetcar passengers mentioned in m63.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD wait for the smaller vehicle to move right BEFORE passing the smaller vehicle WHEN the driver is making a left turn behind the smaller vehicle

sources.quote: Wait for the smaller vehicle to move right before you pass.

statements.note: The condition 'making a left turn behind one of these vehicles' is inferred from the context of the 'Left turns' section and the subsequent passages c6 and c7 which describe the same scenario.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pull up beside the vehicle ahead to make the left turn at the same time WHEN the driver is making a left turn behind the vehicle ahead

sources.quote: If you are making a left turn behind one of these vehicles, do not pull up beside it to make your turn at the same time.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD stay behind the vehicle ahead AND turn WHEN the driver is making a left turn behind the vehicle ahead AND the way is [?clear]

sources.quote: Stay behind and turn when the way is clear.

flags.note: No objective measure for when the way is clear is given.

statements.note: The condition 'making a left turn behind one of these vehicles' is inferred from the context of the 'Left turns' section and the preceding passage c6.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT use a left-turn lane for passing

sources.quote: These left-turn lanes are not to be used for passing.

flags.note: The phrase 'not to be used' is a prohibition, but without explicit legal wording like 'illegal' or 'must not', it is treated as strong advice.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD keep to the right WHEN driving along a freeway

sources.quote: Traffic should keep to the right, using the left lanes for passing.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD use the left lanes for passing WHEN driving along a freeway

sources.quote: Traffic should keep to the right, using the left lanes for passing.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD use the far left lane of a multi-lane freeway to pass traffic moving slower than the speed limit WHEN driving along a freeway

sources.quote: Use the far left lane of a multi-lane freeway to pass traffic moving slower than the speed limit, but don't stay there.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT stay in the far left lane of a multi-lane freeway WHEN driving along a freeway

sources.quote: Use the far left lane of a multi-lane freeway to pass traffic moving slower than the speed limit, but don't stay there.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD drive in the right-hand lane WHEN driving along a freeway AND it is possible

sources.quote: Drive in the right-hand lane when possible.

statements.text: a driver of a large truck MUST NOT travel in the far left lane WHEN driving on a freeway with three or more lanes in each direction

sources.quote: On many freeways with three or more lanes in each direction, large trucks cannot travel in the far left lane and must use the lane to the right for passing.

flags.note: The rule applies to 'many' such freeways, implying not all, but the specific criteria for which freeways are not detailed.

statements.text: a driver of a large truck MUST use the lane to the right of the far left lane for passing WHEN driving on a freeway with three or more lanes in each direction

sources.quote: On many freeways with three or more lanes in each direction, large trucks cannot travel in the far left lane and must use the lane to the right for passing.

flags.note: The rule applies to 'many' such freeways, implying not all, but the specific criteria for which freeways are not detailed.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD drive in the right lane WHEN driving along a freeway

sources.quote: Get into the habit of driving in the right lane, leaving the other lanes clear for passing.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD leave the other lanes clear for passing WHEN driving along a freeway

sources.quote: Get into the habit of driving in the right lane, leaving the other lanes clear for passing.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass another vehicle WHEN driving in fog

sources.quote: Avoid passing, changing lanes and crossing traffic.
Don't pass other vehicles or speed up suddenly.

statements.note: m45 and m47 both advise against passing in fog. m47 also advises against speeding up suddenly, which is not part of the passing topic.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass another vehicle WHEN driving in a whiteout

sources.quote: Avoid passing, changing lanes and crossing traffic.
Don't attempt to pass a vehicle moving slowly or speed up to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely.

statements.note: m48 and m49 both advise against passing in a whiteout. m49 also advises against speeding up to get away from a close follower, which is not part of the passing topic.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT speed up to pass a vehicle moving slowly WHEN driving in fog

sources.quote: Don't speed up to pass a vehicle moving slowly or to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely.

statements.note: This is a specific instance of passing (speeding up to overtake). The alternative purpose (getting away from a close follower) is not passing.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT speed up to pass a vehicle moving slowly WHEN driving in a whiteout

sources.quote: Don't attempt to pass a vehicle moving slowly or speed up to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely.

statements.note: This is a specific instance of passing (speeding up to overtake). The alternative purpose (getting away from a close follower) is not passing.

statements.text: FACT on freeways, several snow plows may be staggered across the road, clearing all lanes at the same time by passing a ridge of snow from plow to plow

sources.quote: On freeways, several snow plows may be staggered across the road, clearing all lanes at the same time by passing a ridge of snow from plow to plow.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass between snow plows WHEN the snow plows are staggered across the road on a freeway BECAUSE there is not enough room to pass safely AND the ridge of wet snow can throw the vehicle out of control

sources.quote: Do not try to pass between them. This is extremely dangerous because there is not enough room to pass safely, and the ridge of wet snow can throw your vehicle out of control.

flags.note: No measure of room is given.

statements.note: The condition 'staggered across the road on a freeway' comes from the preceding sentence describing the plow configuration.

statements.force_from: context (Regulatory signs: "These signs give a direction that must be obeyed")
statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass on a road WHEN a "do not pass" sign is posted for the road

sources.quote: a regulatory sign
Do not pass on this road.

statements.note: The legal force comes from the Regulatory signs section introduction, which states these signs must be obeyed.

statements.force_from: context (Regulatory signs: "These signs give a direction that must be obeyed")
statements.text: a driver MUST keep right WHEN driving slow traffic on a multi-lane road

sources.quote: Slow traffic on multi-lane roads must keep right.
a regulatory sign

statements.note: The role is 'a driver' because the rule applies to the driver of the slow traffic.

statements.force_from: context (Regulatory signs: "These signs give a direction that must be obeyed")
statements.text: a driver MUST keep to the right lane WHEN driving on a road with multiple lanes UNLESS the driver is passing on a two-lane section where climbing or passing lanes are provided

sources.quote: a regulatory sign
Keep to the right lane except when passing on two-lane sections where climbing or passing lanes are provided.

statements.note: The exception is in the same passage, so it is an UNLESS clause.

statements.text: FACT the downward lines on a warning sign show the side on which a driver may safely pass

sources.quote: The downward lines show the side on which you may safely pass.

flags.note: The sign indicates the side for safe passing, but 'safe' is a judgment call based on conditions.

statements.force_from: context (Temporary condition signs: implied legal force for temporary traffic control)
statements.text: a driver MUST NOT pass a pilot vehicle or pace vehicle WHEN the vehicle is bearing a temporary condition sign that prohibits passing

sources.quote: a temporary condition sign
Do not pass the pilot vehicle or pace vehicle bearing this sign.

statements.note: The force is inferred from the context of temporary condition signs, which are typically regulatory in nature.

statements.text: DEFINE long commercial vehicle (LCV) IS a double trailer THAT can be up to 40 m in length

sources.quote: This placard indicates a long commercial vehicle, which is a double trailer and can be up to 40 metres in length.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD recognize a long commercial vehicle (LCV) on the highway AND SHOULD anticipate the extended length and limited speed WHEN preparing to pass one on the highway

sources.quote: Long commercial vehicle (LCV)
It is important to be able to recognize an LCV on the highway, based on rear signage, and anticipate both the extended length and limited speed when preparing to pass one on the highway.

statements.note: The force is advisory because the handbook uses 'It is important to' and 'anticipate', which are recommendations rather than legal duties.

statements.text: FACT pavement markings tell a driver when it is not safe to pass

sources.quote: Pavement markings divide traffic lanes, show turning lanes, mark pedestrian crossings, indicate obstacles and tell you when it is not safe to pass.

statements.force_from: text ("means it is unsafe to pass")
statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass WHEN a solid line is at the left of the driver's lane BECAUSE it is unsafe to pass

sources.quote: A solid line at the left of your lane means it is unsafe to pass.
vehicles travelling beside a solid yellow line

flags.note: The handbook states the condition is unsafe, which implies a prohibition, but does not explicitly state a legal penalty or use 'must not'.

statements.note: The phrase 'means it is unsafe' is treated as advice (SHOULD NOT) because the handbook does not explicitly label it as a legal prohibition with a penalty in this passage, though it is a strong safety warning.

statements.text: a driver MAY pass WHEN a broken line is at the left of the driver's lane AND the way is clear AND there are enough broken lines ahead to complete the pass safely

sources.quote: A broken line at the left of your lane means you may pass if the way is clear. ('A' may pass if there are enough broken lines ahead to complete the pass safely.)
vehicles travelling beside broken yellow lines

flags.note: The driver must judge whether the way is clear.
The driver must judge if there are enough broken lines to complete the pass safely.

statements.note: The permission 'may pass' is explicit in the text.

statements.text: a driver MUST slow down AND carefully pass a stopped emergency vehicle IF VIOLATED 3 demerit points

sources.quote: Failing to slow and carefully pass a stopped emergency vehicle

flags.note: No specific measure for careful passing is given.

statements.note: The penalty for failing to do this makes the action a legal duty.

statements.text: a driver MUST move into another lane WHEN passing a stopped emergency vehicle ONLY IF it is possible IF VIOLATED 3 demerit points

sources.quote: Failing to move, where possible, into another lane when passing a stopped emergency vehicle

flags.note: The driver must judge whether moving is possible.

statements.note: The penalty for failing to do this makes the action a legal duty.

statements.text: FACT driving a motor vehicle to prevent another vehicle from passing is a dangerous behaviour

sources.quote: driving a motor vehicle to prevent another vehicle from passing

statements.note: The heading 'Sanctions – dangerous behaviours' provides the context that this action is classified as a dangerous behaviour subject to sanctions, but the specific sanction is not detailed in this passage.

statements.text: FACT a driver towing a trailer cannot accelerate as quickly AND needs more space BECAUSE the length of the vehicle is much longer with a trailer attached

sources.quote: You cannot accelerate as quickly when you are towing a trailer. You also need more space because the length of your vehicle is much longer with a trailer attached.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD ensure the driver has [?enough] time and room to complete the pass BEFORE passing

sources.quote: Before you pass, make sure you have enough time and room to complete the pass.

flags.note: No specific measure of time or room is given.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD allow [?more] room before moving back to the lane AFTER passing

sources.quote: Once you have passed, allow more room before you move back to your lane.

flags.note: No specific amount of extra room is defined.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD NOT cut back into the lane too soon AFTER passing BECAUSE it can cause the trailer to sway and make it difficult to control

sources.quote: Do not cut back into the lane too soon. This can cause your trailer to sway and make it difficult to control.

flags.note: No specific time or distance is given for when it is safe to cut back.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD signal AND pull over AND let the other vehicles pass WHEN the driver is holding up a line of traffic

sources.quote: If you are holding up a line of traffic, signal, pull over and let the other vehicles pass.

statements.text: FACT fast-moving trucks and buses create a strong air disturbance behind them

sources.quote: Fast-moving trucks and buses create a strong air disturbance behind them.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD NOT brake WHEN the trailer is whipped to the side by the air disturbance of a passing large bus or truck

sources.quote: If a large bus or truck passes you, the wall of wind behind it may whip your trailer to the side, pushing it out of control. When you experience this, do not brake.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer SHOULD carefully steer the vehicle and trailer back into position WHEN the trailer is whipped to the side by the air disturbance of a passing large bus or truck

sources.quote: When you experience this, do not brake. Carefully steer your vehicle and trailer back into position.

statements.text: a driver towing a trailer MAY increase speed slightly WHEN the trailer is whipped to the side by the air disturbance of a passing large bus or truck

sources.quote: A slight increase in speed may help.

flags.note: The handbook states this as a possibility/advice, not a legal permission or duty.

statements.note: The phrase 'may help' indicates a potential benefit rather than a legal permission, so the force is ambiguous between advice and permission; MAY is used to reflect the permissive language, but the M flag notes the advisory nature.

statements.text: a driver MUST move to the right AND allow the other vehicle to pass WHEN the driver of another vehicle is about to overtake and pass the driver's vehicle

sources.quote: When the driver of another vehicle is about to overtake and pass your vehicle, you must:
Move to the right and allow such vehicle to pass.

statements.note: The lead sentence (m87) provides the condition and the legal force ("must"); the item (m88) provides the specific action.
